title: Integrating SentinelOne with Zero Trust Branch

blocks.text: Zero Trust Branch integrates with SentinelOne to provide unified visibility, control, and automated threat response across distributed enterprise environments. You can extend endpoint intelligence into network and branch-level security decisions with an API-based, policy-driven framework.

Zero Trust Branch leverages SentinelOne’s real-time endpoint telemetry and threat intelligence to enhance asset awareness and security posture within the branch. SentinelOne provides detailed device attributes, threat indicators, and behavioral data that enrich Zero Trust Branch's asset inventory and policy engines. Zero Trust Branch enforces segmentation, quarantine, or policy adjustments at the network level based on SentinelOne’s risk scores and incident detections.

This integration simplifies security management, enhances automation and response accuracy, and offers a complete zero trust posture to prevent lateral movement, minimize attack surfaces, and provide continuous verification across all assets, users, and applications.

blocks.heading: Integrating SentinelOne with Zero Trust Branch

blocks.text: Follow these steps to integrate SentinelOne with Zero Trust Branch:

blocks.item: 1. Generate the SentinelOne API token.
Log in to the SentinelOne portal.
Go to Settings > Users > Actions > Add New User.
See image.
In the Add a new user window:
Enter the Full Name and Email Address for the account.
For Role, select Viewer from the drop-down menu.
Click Save.
See image.
A new user link is sent to the email address mentioned in the previous step.
Open the email and click the new user link to confirm the account creation, and then enter a strong password for the user account.
Log in to the SentinelOne portal as the new user and accept the end user license agreement (EULA).
In the top-right corner, click your profile name and select My User.
See image.
Go to Action > API Token Operation > Generate API token.
Enter the two-factor authentication code when prompted, then click Confirm Action.
See image.
An API token displays. Click Copy API Token to copy the API token to the clipboard, then click Close.
See image.
The SentinelOne API token is now ready for use.
2. Integrate the API token with Zero Trust Branch.
From the navigation menu, go to Zero Trust Branch > Resources > Integrations.
On the Integrations page, click Settings under SentinelOne Integration.
See image.
In the SentinelOne Integration drawer:
Enter the API Token that you previously copied, and the Base URL.
Next, click Test to verify the details.
See image.
A confirmation message appears indicating that the API token and Base URL are configured correctly.
Click Save.
3. Set up the SentinelOne agent.
To download the SentinelOne agent:
In the left-side navigation of the SentinelOne portal, click Settings > SITES.
See image.
The list of sites displays on the Settings page.
In the Name column, click the site name to go to the SENTINELS page.
See image.
On the SENTINELS page, click the PACKAGES tab, then click the Download icon to download the required agent.
See image.
On your Linux host system, open the terminal and run the following commands to install the agent:

-rw-rw-r-- 1 admin60 admin60 60786350 Oct 14 18:09 SentinelAgent_linux_x86_64_v25_2_2_14.deb admin60@pod-60-lnx-b:~/Downloads$ admin60@pod-60-lnx-b:~/Downloads$ sudo dpkg -i SentinelAgent_linux_x86_64_v25_2_2_14.deb [sudo] password for admin60: Selecting previously unselected package sentinelagent. (Reading database ... 276178 files and directories currently installed.) Preparing to unpack SentinelAgent_linux_x86_64_V25_2_2_14.deb ... Unpacking sentinelagent (25.2.2.14) ... Setting up sentinelagent (25.2.2.14) ...
Set the SentinelOne URL and the site token:
sudo /opt/sentinelone/bin/sentinelctl management url set <sentinelone_URL> sudo /opt/sentinelone/bin/sentinelctl management token set '<site_token>'
Start the service and check the agent's status.
4. Verify the SentinelOne endpoints.
In the left-side navigation of the SentinelOne portal, click Settings > SITES.
In the Name column, click the site name to go to the SENTINELS page.
On the SENTINELS page, click the ENDPOINTS tab to view the list of endpoints.
See image.
Click the required device name.
A drawer appears. By default, the GENERAL tab is selected and you can view the device details.
See image.
5. Verify the integration.
In the Zscaler Admin Console, go to Zero Trust Branch > Dashboard > Asset Intelligence.
On the Assets page, and in the Device column, click the required device name.
See image.
A drawer appears.
Click the SentinelOne tab and verify the integration details.
See image.
